notes: Fresh check for the Tasmania (MRT) geochemistry and drill-hole load of 2026-11-02. Not part of the gate.

questions.q: Where are the strongest tin anomalies in Tasmania's stream sediment data?
questions.judge: Uses the Tasmanian (Mineral Resources Tasmania) stream-sediment samples, reports anomalous areas with sample counts, distinguishes new leads from areas near known tin occurrences or deposits, and credits Mineral Resources Tasmania. It must not present drill-hole assays as stream-sediment anomalies. Says anomalies are not deposits.

questions.q: What are the best copper intervals in drill hole DD97BC9 at Balfour, and who drilled it?

truth.max_cu: SELECT max(w.cu_p) FROM geochem.sample_chemistry_wide w JOIN drilling.drillholes h USING (drillhole_id) WHERE h.hole_name = 'DD97BC9'

questions.judge: Lists the highest copper intervals with their depths (from-to, metres), the top one about 5.34% Cu (53,400 ppm), names Rio Tinto Exploration as the company, and credits Mineral Resources Tasmania. Does not invent intervals or a resource.

questions.q: How many drill holes do you have in Tasmania, and what drilling methods were used?

truth.holes: SELECT count(*) FROM drilling.drillholes WHERE source_system = 'AUSTRALIA_TAS_MRT'

questions.judge: States 34,871 drill holes (open-file data from Mineral Resources Tasmania, to February 2023) with a breakdown by drill type (diamond the largest, then auger, percussion, RC, air core, rotary ...) whose parts are consistent with the total, and credits MRT.
